articles.title: A.J. Brown's knee report takes unexpected turn as $25 million payment dispute raises fresh questions about his exit
articles.summary: New England Patriots are still waiting for A.J.
articles.body: New England Patriots are still waiting for A.J. Brown to make a meaningful impact, but head coach Mike Vrabel has offered a different explanation for why the wide receiver left Tennessee in 2022. Asked whether the Titans had concerns about Brown's knees before trading him, Vrabel pointed to a contract dispute involving the franchise's ownership. His comments have brought the $25 million annual figure back into focus and raised fresh questions about the decisions behind Brown's departure from Tennessee.Mike Vrabel points to money behind A.J. Brown's Titans exitVrabel addressed the subject during an appearance on WEEI's "The Greg Hill Show" on Monday. The question referred to a report claiming doctors had warned Tennessee's leadership in 2022 that Brown's knee had only two years left.It also asked whether that medical assessment influenced the ownership's decision to trade him and whether Vrabel knew about the concerns at the time.The Patriots coach did not accept that explanation. Instead, he pointed directly to the financial disagreement that surrounded Brown's contract situation.“No, the owner didn’t want to pay A.J. Brown 25 million dollars,” Vrabel said. “That’s what it was.”Vrabel also brought up Brown's availability during his time with the Philadelphia Eagles, suggesting that his injury history did not tell the complete story behind Tennessee's decision.“He went to Philly, and I mean, A.J. has participated in quite a handful of games; and has missed a few since he went to Philly,” Vrabel said.The Titans traded Brown to Philadelphia during the 2022 NFL Draft. In return, Tennessee received the 18th and 101st overall picks. Brown then signed a four-year, $100 million extension with the Eagles, putting his average annual salary at $25 million.His production offered little reason to question the move from Philadelphia's perspective. Brown recorded more than 1,000 receiving yards in each of his first four seasons with the Eagles. He also played all 17 regular-season games in both 2022 and 2023, before appearing in 13 games in 2024 and 15 in 2025.Patriots still waiting for Brown to deliver after tradeVrabel now has Brown in New England, but the early returns have been far from what the Patriots hoped to get from the receiver. The franchise acquired him on June 1, sending a 2028 first-round pick and a 2027 fifth-round pick to Philadelphia.Brown has managed just 11 receptions for 128 yards and no touchdowns across four games. His latest outing against the Detroit Lions brought only two catches for 27 yards.That production is a concern for a Patriots team that invested significant draft capital to bring him in. However, Vrabel suggested that Brown's current struggles were not something the coaching staff expected after watching him during the summer.“But by all indications, unfortunately, after the training camp that he had, I wouldn’t have anticipated anything,” he said.The coach also described the setbacks Brown has faced, including getting rolled up on during the season opener and being dragged down during his latest injury incident.Vrabel did not offer a timeline for his return. The Patriots will have to wait until Brown is healthy enough to contribute again.“So we’ll just keep trying to get him healthy and whenever he can get back out there to help us, I know that he will.”For Vrabel, the current priority is getting Brown back on the field. But his comments have also reopened an old debate about whether Tennessee's decision was driven by concerns over his knees or an unwillingness to meet his contract demands.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: ‘Tyreek Hill’s back’ – Kansas City Chiefs breakout star reminds me of former wide receiver, says Mike Florio
articles.summary: The Kansas City Chiefs’ offense has stepped up a level over the past two weeks, with Patrick Mahomes throwing eight touchdown passes. The running game has al...
articles.body:
The Kansas City Chiefs' offense has stepped up a level over the past two weeks, with Patrick Mahomes throwing eight touchdown passes.

The running game has also had a different look, rookie Emmett Johnson has stepped into the backfield with Kenneth Walker dealing with an injury.

Johnson had 105 rushing yards in Week 11 and one touchdown, plus a further 38 receiving yards from four targets.

The rookie wears the Chiefs' number 10 jersey once worn by wide receiver Tyreek Hill, and Mike Florio sees similarities with his burst of pace.

Speaking to Pro Football Talk, Florio explained: "You've got to use him. I mean, people see that number 10, and I've heard people say it's Isiah Pacheco.

"When I see him running in the open field, I'm thinking Tyreek Hill's back, it is just the weirdest thing to see.

"But he is extremely effective, and there are teams out there kicking themselves that they didn't draft him when they could."

How Johnson's 40 yard dash compares to Tyreek Hill

Tyreek Hill was also a fifth-round draft pick for the Kansas City Chiefs, 10 years earlier. He went on to win one Super Bowl with Patrick Mahomes, before forcing an exit to sign with the Miami Dolphins.

Hill, 32, is attempting to recover from a serious knee injury and wants to revive his NFL career.

He was renowned as the fastest player in the NFL, and Florio's comparison is a major compliment for Emmett Johnson and his own ability to run into space with the ball.

Tyreek Hill did not participate at the NFL Combine, but set a 4.29 time at the 40-yard dash at his West Alabama Pro Day.

Emmett Johnson's dash time was an unimpressive 4.56 seconds, which also helps to explain why he fell to the fifth round.

The Chiefs still saw something special in him, and Johnson is proving it on the field where it really matters.

articles.title: "Just having that camera on me at all times": Travis Kelce revealed the surprising role Donna Kelce's home videos played in building his confidence
articles.summary: Travis Kelce's confidence in front of millions of people did not develop overnight.
articles.body: Travis Kelce's confidence in front of millions of people did not develop overnight. Long before the Kansas City Chiefs star became a familiar face on television, he had an unexpected advantage at home. His mother, Donna Kelce, loved recording family moments, and those childhood videos helped him become comfortable around cameras. During a press conference on February 2, 2024, ahead of Super Bowl LVIII, Travis opened up about how Donna's simple habit influenced his personality and why sports eventually helped him overcome his childhood shyness.How Donna Kelce's home videos helped Travis build confidenceWhen reporters asked Travis Kelce about his ease in front of cameras, he immediately credited his mother. Rather than pointing to his NFL career or years of media training, the tight end looked back at his childhood."My mom’s home videos, man," Travis said during the February 2, 2024 press conference.He explained that Donna frequently recorded him while he was growing up, making cameras a familiar part of his everyday life."Just having that camera on me at all times, seeing what silly stuff I'm gonna do next, man," he added.The experience appeared to remove some of the discomfort that many people feel when they are being filmed. Travis said he had always felt comfortable in different settings and found it easy to look into a camera."Honestly, I've always been comfortable in the rooms that I've been in and just been fortunate that I've been able to kind of look into a camera with ease, I guess."For Donna, recording her children was a way to preserve family memories. However, those videos also gave Travis years of exposure to cameras before his professional career brought constant public attention.Travis Kelce revealed how sports helped him overcome childhood shynessInterestingly, Travis did not credit home videos alone for shaping his confidence. He also spoke about how playing sports helped him become more expressive.Despite his outgoing personality today, the NFL star admitted that he was quite different as a child."You probably won't believe it, but I was a shy kid growing up until I got onto the sports field or the court or the ice rink," he explained.According to Travis, competing gave him an environment where he could relax, enjoy himself and show more of his personality. Success on the field gradually strengthened his belief in himself."I was having success, and that just kind of propelled me to have confidence in life," he said.Those experiences became particularly relevant as his career expanded beyond football. From hosting Saturday Night Live in March 2023 to appearing in television commercials and entertainment projects, Travis embraced opportunities that placed him in front of new audiences.His February 2024 admission offered an interesting reminder that the personality fans now recognise had developed through years of small experiences. Donna's home videos and his love for sports both played a part in that journey.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: From a $200 signing deal to a $3.1 million auction record: How Tom Brady's rookie card became a collector's treasure
articles.summary: Tom Brady's legendary NFL career eventually turned him into one of the most valuable names in sports memorabilia.
articles.body: Tom Brady's legendary NFL career eventually turned him into one of the most valuable names in sports memorabilia. But his first trading card deal was hardly a million-dollar opportunity. When the future seven-time Super Bowl champion entered the league as the 199th overall pick in 2000, he was happy to earn a few hundred dollars for signing cards. More than two decades later, those same signatures became highly sought-after collectibles. In 2021, two copies of his rookie card made auction history, with one fetching more than $3.1 million.Tom Brady's $200 rookie card deal became a million-dollar collectibleBefore becoming an NFL icon, Tom Brady had little reason to imagine that his signature would one day command millions. His agent, Steve, brought him a trading card opportunity early in his career. The offer involved signing 1,000 cards for 20 cents each.Brady recalled the conversation during an appearance on Good Morning America in April 2021.“My agent, Steve, was like, ‘Got a trading card deal for you. You sign a thousand cards and they’re gonna pay you like 20 cents a card,'” Brady said. “Twenty cents a card? I’m gonna be rich!”The arrangement earned him just $200. However, the value of his autograph changed dramatically as his career took off. By 2021, Brady had won seven Super Bowls, including his first championship with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. Collectors were also spending record amounts on rare football cards.A copy of his 2000 Playoff Contenders Championship Rookie Ticket autograph card sold for $1.32 million in March 2021. Fitbit CEO James Park purchased that edition, but another sale soon pushed the record much higher.Tom Brady rookie card shattered auction records in 2021On April 2, 2021, Lelands auctioned another copy of the same card, numbered 99 out of just 100 produced. The card had spent years in a private collection after being purchased on eBay more than a decade earlier.Bidding opened at $75,000. After 67 bids, an anonymous buyer paid $2,252,854, setting a new public auction record for a football card.Another collector, who owned a copy he believed was in better condition, saw an opportunity to surpass that figure.Lelands director of acquisitions Jordan Gilroy explained the buyer's motivation to The Washington Times.“He wanted to use the momentum of us setting that initial world record and essentially break it,” Gilroy said.The strategy worked. On June 4, 2021, the collector's card sold for $3,107,372 at Lelands' Mid-Spring Classic. Beckett graded it Mint 9, while its autograph received a perfect 10.Although a one-of-one Patrick Mahomes card reportedly fetched $4.3 million in a private sale later, Brady's June 2021 transaction remained a landmark public auction result.For Brady, those early $200 earnings became a remarkable reminder of how much his name and signature had grown in value.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Packers star Micah Parsons reportedly cleared to return from ACL injury, will make season debut vs. Rams on Thanksgiving Eve
articles.summary: Micah Parsons has been recovering from a torn ACL and meniscus in his left knee for nearly a full year.
articles.body:
The Green Bay Packers star pass rusher has been cleared to return and will make his season debut in their Thanksgiving Eve matchup with the Los Angeles Rams, according to NFL Network's Ian Rapoport .

It will mark Parsons' first NFL game since he tore his left ACL and meniscus last season. He went down with the knee injury in their loss to the Denver Broncos on Dec. 14 , and has been sidelined recovering ever since. The Packers lost four straight games after losing Parsons, including a playoff loss to the Chicago Bears.

Parsons had 12.5 sacks in his 14 games with the Packers last season, and had accounted for a third of Green Bay's pressures before he went down. It was his first campaign with the team after they acquired him in a deal with the Dallas Cowboys just ahead of Week 1.

Parsons was cleared to return to practice earlier this month and started his ramp-up while targeting Wednesday's game at SoFi Stadium for his return. Clearly, that has gone exactly to plan.

"I feel like I've done everything I possibly could to put myself in position to potentially play on Wednesday, but for sure this season," Parsons said on Monday afternoon before meeting with team doctors, via The Athletic's Matt Schneidman . "I'll be looking forward to returning to the field."

The Packers will enter Wednesday with a 6-4 record, which has them in last in the NFC North but very much alive in the playoff conversation. They were off last week, but went into their bye fresh off a rough 30-10 loss to the Minnesota Vikings.

While it's been almost a full year since he's played in a game, Parsons is more than ready to get back. And he's well aware of what a win over the Rams would do for the Packers' postseason hopes entering the final stretch of the season.

"I'm really geeked up," he said, via ESPN's Rob Demovsky. "They're like, 'Are you nervous?' I'm just so focused, I'm so locked in on what's ahead of me. I understand what this game Wednesday means to the organization, myself and what it means for playoffs. If I can be out there, I want to be out there."

articles.title: David Bailey already drawing Hall of Fame comparison 10 games into Jets career
articles.summary: Davis said Bailey has only scratched the surface of what he can do.
articles.body:
Demario Davis is in his 15th NFL season, and he has played with some greats.

The Jets linebacker sees traits in rookie edge rusher David Bailey that he has observed in some of those great ones. Davis praised Bailey's "process" on Monday, saying the rookie does not let outside factors affect his preparation routine, similarly to the best players he has been around.

"I don't know what all goes into his process, but I know I see him in the same spots around the building all the time," Davis said. "That type of stuff is what I've seen from guys who are now in the Hall of Fame. When you come in and you go through the week, you see them in the same spots in the building all the time, whether it was an All-Pro wide receiver or an All-Pro running back or an All-Pro quarterback, an All-Pro defensive end in Cam Jordan — a solidified Hall of Famer, one of the best I've ever seen do it — it's all about that process. Those guys have a regimen and a routine that doesn't change based on what's going on around them. That's very rare to see for a rookie."

Bailey has been a star on the field. He added two sacks against the Chargers to bring his season total to 9 ½, just shy of Hugh Douglas' Jets rookie record of 10 set in 1995. He is five away from Jevon Kearse's NFL rookie record of 14 ½, established in 1999.

Davis said Bailey has only scratched the surface of what he can do.

"He's only going to get better," the veteran linebacker said. "It's going to be scary for a lot of quarterbacks for a long time and it's going to be good for the Jets for a long time."

The Jets gave up a touchdown just before halftime Sunday when Chargers quarterback Justin Herbert ran for a 10-yard score as time expired. The Jets showed an interesting defense on the play, with three players rushing and eight players lined up on the goal line. Herbert took off, and the Jets could not bring him down. If they had tackled him, the Chargers might have been unable to even kick a field goal. Both Dane Belton and Davis missed tackles on the play.

"They had a chance to try to score on a throwing play and we had guys in the end zone," head coach Aaron Glenn said, "but then again, if he had a chance to run it, we had guys able to converge on the ball and I think if you look at that play, I think we had two missed tackles, which would've put them in a tough situation with six seconds to try to run the ball in that situation. The thing is we just got to make that tackle. We make that tackle; we put ourselves in a good position."

articles.title: Dan Orlovsky stumped by Mina Kimes’ Alamo reference
articles.summary: Dan Orlovsky is an NFL analyst across ESPN platforms, most prominently on the award-winning NFL Live. He’s also a professional oversharer. Orlovsky has made...
articles.body:
Dan Orlovsky is an NFL analyst across ESPN platforms, most prominently on the award-winning NFL Live . He's also a professional oversharer.

Orlovsky has made a habit out of captivating the nation with his unique habits , leading to a bland grilled chicken birthday cake , and his character arc regarding pedicures .

Just in the past month, Orlovsky asked The Pat McAfee Show crew whether it's possible to walk from Alaska to Russia, declared himself a non-smoker (and threw his poor wife under the bus) on NFL Live , and learned live on national television what percent means.

Now, the history of the Alamo isn't common knowledge like the definition of percent, but it also flew over Orlovsky's head.

On Sunday, Orlovsky tweeted , "The Texans are alive." On Monday, Mina Kimes, Orlovsky's NFL Live colleague, reposted it and quipped , "General Santa Anna on the morning of March 6, 1836."

Orlovsky replied, "Wtf this mean," and Kimes had the perfect meme prepared to put a bow on this whole exchange:

Leave it to Kimes, recent champion of Celebrity Jeopardy! All Stars , to turn Orlovsky's very basic Houston Texans tweet into a history lesson on Antonio Lopez de Santa Anna and the Texas Revolution.

It is always possible that Orlovsky was joking, but given his track record of earnest unawareness, it's more likely that Kimes' joke flew over his head. But honestly, in a sports media landscape littered with know-it-alls, we would all be better off if more people were willing to simply ask, "Wtf this mean."

articles.title: Bengals safety Bryan Cook injures ankle vs Commanders Monday night
articles.summary: Bengals safety Bryan Cook hurt his ankle during the team's NFL Week 11 game against Washington on Monday night.
articles.body:
Cincinnati Bengals safety Bryan Cook injured his right ankle during the second quarter of the team's NFL Week 11 game against the Washington Commanders on ESPN's Monday Night Football at Northwest Stadium.

Cook walked off the field to the sideline under his own power.

The Bengals announced that Cook's return is questionable.

"It looked like it was gonna be a lot worse," MNF analyst Troy Aikman said during the broadcast. "Definitely a good sign to see him walking off (the field)."

Cook was hurt after he was in on a sack of Ravens quarterback Tyler "Snoop" Huntley during the team's NFL Week 7 rout in Baltimore. Cook got up and walked slowly off the field, and returned to the game later in the fourth quarter.

Cook hurt his ankle during the first quarter of the team's NFL Week 3 loss in Pittsburgh. Cook missed two games because of the injury.

See photos from Bengals vs. Commanders on Monday Night Football

Cook, a former Mount Healthy High School standout and Cincinnati Bearcats defensive back, was on the sideline after having his ankle taped during the Steelers' second scoring drive of the game. Cook returned to the game early in the second quarter.

Cook agreed to terms March 9 on a reported three-year deal worth $40.25 million.

"My family's been talking about this for a long time," Cook said March 12. "Being able to come back home and … be closer to our family. I'm just excited for the opportunity, excited for the new chapter in my life."

Cook was at Kansas City's T-Mobile Center to watch the ninth-seeded Bearcats ' men's basketball team defeat No. 16 seed Utah in the Big 12 tournament.

Cook starred at UC from 2019 to 2021 before becoming a second-round pick of the Chiefs in 2022.
